text:
incident-bot: :pager: P1 Alert — tenant: oceana-prod (dedicated pool dp-7, vpc vpc-02)
incident-bot: billing-monitor detected token_count anomaly: daily tokens ↑ 5.2x; per-request token spikes observed (~50k+ tokens/request). Rate limits triggered and billing alarms fired. Pager routed to on-call.

maria_oncall: acked — taking lead. tagging eng-sre and eng-ml. any initial impact notes from customer side? @josh_am can you confirm if this is an active contract customer?

josh_am: yes, Oceana Health (enterprise, dedicated pool). They have an active support SLA. I’ll join the loop. CSM is liz_cs.

maria_oncall: timeline so far — alerts started 08:40 UTC. Our autoscale handled throughput but billing exposure is high. I’m going to grab logs and tenant request samples.

kevin_sre: grabbing request samples from dp-7 gateway. running quick query:

```
# example kinesis query (pseudo)
select tenant_id, request_id, token_count, sample_text[1:200]
from requests
where pool = "dp-7" and ts >= 1925007600
order by token_count desc
limit 20
```

kevin_sre: output snippet (sanitized):

```
tenant    request_id        token_count    sample_prefix
oceana    r_9a7f3b         50123          "VFZlciB..."  # base64-like prefix
oceana    r_9a7f9d         48612          "\ud83d\ude0a\ud83d\ude0a..."
oceana    r_9aa0c1         47200          "<html>\n\u00a0..."
```

kevin_sre: first two look weird — first sample appears base64-blob prepended to prompt, second has repeated emoji codepoints escaped, third has a bunch of non-breaking spaces.

anya_ml: jumping in — initial hypothesis: tokenizer/encoding mismatch + client-side encoding change. If a client sends UTF-16LE bytes to a byte-level BPE tokenizer that expects UTF-8, tokenization will diverge and often inflate token counts (every code unit can map to separate bytes/tokens). Also embedding base64 or binary blobs inline massively increases tokenization.

anya_ml: I ran a repro locally on a short snippet showing the effect:

```
# python (+ tiktoken-like pseudo)
text = "Hello 🌊"
# utf-8 token count
tokens_utf8 = encode_bpe(text.encode('utf-8'))  # => 3 tokens
# simulate client sending UTF-16LE bytes interpreted as utf-8
bytes_utf16 = text.encode('utf-16le')
tokens_misdecoded = encode_bpe(bytes_utf16)  # => many more tokens
print(tokens_utf8, tokens_misdecoded)
```

anya_ml: result: 3 vs 34 tokens in small test. scale that up and you blow past quota/billing thresholds.

maria_oncall: good find. do we have a change on client SDKs or customer deploys around 08:30–08:40?

josh_am: I pinged Oceana's engineering lead (via the support channel) and they confirmed a front-end rollback earlier today. They said they shipped a patch to the JS SDK to enable "richText" mode around 08:20 UTC. They think it only affects display. CSM on call now.

liz_cs: I’m on the customer call — their dev says the new patch changed how the client serializes text for legacy mobile bridges (it toggles on UTF-16LE serialization for iOS). They didn’t realize our ingestion expects UTF-8 normalized. Customer is apologetic and wants a fast mitigation.

kevin_sre: mitigation options (short term):
- apply a temporary per-tenant token cap (hard cap) to stop runaway billing.
- drop or truncate payloads containing long base64 blobs before tokenization at gateway (safe-mode sanitize).
- fallback to lightweight normalization (attempt to decode bytes as UTF-16LE -> re-encode as UTF-8) for oceana-prod only.

maria_oncall: prioritize: 1) hard cap to stop billing ramp, 2) gateway normalization as hotfix, 3) longer-term SDK/contract fix + monitoring.

deploy-bot: runbook-trigger: applied tenant token hard cap 60k/request to oceana-prod — SUCCESS (actioned by maria_oncall).

maria_oncall: confirming hard cap applied. billing alarms suppressed for new spikes; still showing existing outstanding usage. Need to patch gateway to normalize incoming payloads and drop binary attachments inside prompts.

anya_ml: I’ll prepare a small normalization patch we can feature-flag for dp-7. It will: NFC normalize unicode, attempt to detect UTF-16LE/BE byte sequences and transcode to UTF-8, and strip base64-looking blobs > 2k chars from prompt before tokenization. This reduces risk of false positives.

kevin_sre: I’ll create a temporary rule to sniff and truncate long base64 segments in the ingress path for oceana-prod only. rolling out now to dp-7 canary.

maria_oncall: timeline — hard cap applied 08:53 UTC, canary normalization rolling (kevin) 09:00 UTC. If canary good for 10m, promote to pool.

josh_am: I’ll notify Oceana that we applied a protective cap and are routing a normalization hotfix. Will ask them to rollback the client patch until we ship SDK/contract fix.

liz_cs: customer agreed to temporarily disable the new "richText" toggle and roll back mobile bridge. They’ll confirm in 10m. Asking for a postmortem and credit discussion.

anya_ml: quick repro notes I’ll include in the incident ticket:
- root cause: client-side switched to UTF-16LE serialization + inline binary/base64 content; our tokenizer pipeline expects UTF-8 byte-level input -> token explosion.
- immediate mitigation: tenant-level hard cap + gateway transcode & sanitization.
- midterm: SDK change to guarantee UTF-8 serialization + server-side defensive normalization (opt-in per-tenant flags).

maria_oncall: assigning follow-ups:
- Kevin: finish canary -> pool-wide roll (INC-192500-01)
- Anya: write normalization hotfix + tests (INC-192500-02)
- Josh/Liz: customer comms & credits (INC-192500-03)
- Ops: billing reconciliation on outstanding token exposure (INC-192500-04)

kevin_sre: canary looks good — 10m no regressions. promoting to dp-7.

deploy-bot: normalization hotfix rolled to dp-7 (canary -> pool) — SUCCESS.

maria_oncall: monitors green, rate of high-token requests dropped to baseline. billing surge contained. marking incident as mitigated. Will keep open for postmortem and follow-ups.

josh_am: scheduling customer debrief with Oceana for 16:00 UTC today.

liz_cs: noted. customer very appreciative of quick response. Asking for a written summary + timeline.

maria_oncall: thanks all — handoff to postmortem owners. closing on-call handoff now. :white_check_mark:

(threads: follow-ups will be tracked in INC-192500-xx ticket numbers)
